newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm, steady except for fuel.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm, steady except for fuel.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to firm on Wednesday, apart from softer fuel oil.
Gas oil gained around $0.50 on firmer IPE futures.

Traders saw good Italian and French demand for low sulphur diesel, with values maintaining the $10/12 premium to heating oil seen in northern Europe. A handy-sized parcel of 0.05 percent sulphur for loading early December in Sicily was sold high quotes fob +$1 for delivery into Trieste, traders said.
Italian demand was seen for a combi of 10,000 tonnes of 0.2 heating oil and 10,000 tonnes of low sulphur diesel around December 20 into Genoa.
French demand was seen for a combi of 20,000 tonnes of diesel and 10,000 tonnes of heating oil loading December 8-12.
Gasoline rose slightly as the arbitrage opened to the U.S. Cargoes were up $4 at $224/$226 cif.
A total 250,000 tonnes was fixed out of the Med and NWE for the U.S. and Colombia in the last week, an Italian trader said. Cat gasoline was seen moving to New York Harbor, she said.
Some Romanian cargoes were available for mid-December, she said. "There is so much product around and local demand isn't there...so it has to go somewhere," she said.
Naphtha ended steady in what was seen as a balanced market. Algeria's Skikda port was still closed but cargoes delayed in loading had homes, traders said.
High sulphur fuel oil was looking weaker with reasonable supplies seen. The much vaunted Romanian demand was assessed to have taken about three cargoes in November, approx 150,000 tonnes.
"I think we are down to about $108 fob Med, there just is not enough support," said one trader.
"People are discreetly offering around their cargoes," said another.
